bearings.paper_claim: Warm-list targeting rule (2014 field experiment, first-year net donations; warm list N=2,354 with 1,180 gift and 1,174 control; 20-fold cross-validated out-of-sample): gift to 33 percent of warm-list individuals; expected net donation 17.61 euro, which is +2.14 (13.8 percent) vs all-gift, +2.20 (14.3 percent) vs no-gift and +2.17 (14.1 percent) vs random-half, all significant at 1 percent (Table 2, Panel B). On the full 2015 follow-up sample (N=3,616): expected 17.16 euro, -0.88 vs all-gift and +0.45 vs no-gift, neither significant (Table 8, Panel B2).
bearings.system_side: fec/engine/optimize.py: lazy greedy allocation of BUDGET (default 2,500,000) in INC (default 500) chunks across members, maximizing modeled winnability in a fixed stance state. The docstring calls the greedy an exact discrete optimum within that state and withholds the fixed-state certificate when a modeled money threshold changes stance. The observations list is reserved and empty; no realized-outcome comparison against uniform, random or no-spend allocation was found.
bearings.transfer_conditions: The transferable part is the evaluation design: benchmark-relative, net-of-cost gains on held-out units under randomized treatment. Effect sizes do not transfer (1.16-euro gift to German church donors in 2014-15, vs PAC dollars to members of Congress). FEC limits and the absence of randomization mean the system cannot replicate the identification. Any optimizer gain stays model-internal and UNVERIFIED (DE-062) until outcomes are scored against a benchmark allocation.
bearings.verifier_note: Paper numbers re-checked against Table 1, Table 2, Table 8 and the Section 5.3 and 5.6 text. Code side re-read: budget and chunk defaults, lazy greedy, fixed-state certificate wording, and no realized-outcome benchmark. The original CELF label is changed to lazy greedy, following the docstring.

bearings.paper_claim: Responsiveness to the gift is heterogeneous and has to be estimated. Causal-forest best linear predictor heterogeneity loading 0.959 (SE 0.710; p 0.088 one-sided) on the warm list and 0.511 (SE 1.069) on the cold list (Table E.3). The 2014 rule applied to a caliper-matched 2015 warm-list sample (radius 0.1, 35.6 percent treated) gave +2.64 vs all-gift and +2.30 vs no-gift. On the full 2015 sample it gave no significant gain. The paper reports significance against no-gift up to caliper radius 0.25 and says effects are not significant above radius 0.1.
bearings.paper_location: Section 5.2 and Table E.3 (p. 21; Appendix p. 12); Section 5.4; Section 5.6 and Figure H.1 (pp. 30-32)
bearings.system_side: c = 1 + 1.0*exp(-max(lean,0)/5.0), with lean = Cook PVI points toward the member's own party (function compet_c). It multiplies effective dollars on both money legs of the flip family; the per-member cap and the pot stay real dollars. The code labels the constants as owner judgment, uncalibrated, with the reciprocity they encode not validated. The dial defaults ON (unset means ON; '0' reverts).
bearings.code_ref: fec/moneyball_core.py:76-93 (Melange repo, read-only); fec/engine/optimize.py:55-63 uses CM
bearings.transfer_conditions: The paper is about method, not legislators or PVI. It shows what establishing heterogeneous dollar effectiveness would require: randomized variation, a heterogeneity test and a transfer check to a new population. It gives no evidence for or against the PVI shape of c. Do not cite it as support for c.
bearings.verifier_note: Formula, constants and default-ON status verified in code. The original bearing said significance against all-gift holds only up to caliper 0.1; the paper does not say that. Corrected to the paper's actual statements. Brain entries D-104 to D-108 were not read in this run.

bearings.paper_claim: Responsiveness to a costly contact is heterogeneous. Warm-list gift effects (2014, first-year net donations) run from -11.59 euro at the 5th percentile to +17.99 euro at the 95th, and 45 percent of warm-list individuals have estimated effects above the 1.16-euro cost (Section 5.2, Figure 2). A rule built on 300-m geospatial counts, distances and elevation (17.40 euro expected net donation) does not significantly differ from the full-covariate rule (17.61 euro; Table 6, column 6 difference -0.22, not significant).
bearings.system_side: potential = (wp x undecided + (1 - wp) x supporter) x (1 + wi x i), with undecided = (1 - |2s - 1|) x t and supporter = s x (1 - t). The weights wp and wi come from a per-district entry; 0.5 is the default used only when that entry names none (DEFAULT_WEIGHTS). The module as read computes a formula and does not estimate contact response; saved walk results are used only to exclude doors already worked.
bearings.transfer_conditions: Applies to individual-level targeting of a costly contact, which is structurally closest to Terrier. The numbers do not transfer: they come from charitable gifts, not canvass persuasion or GOTV. A learned rule would need randomized contact assignment, such as held-out control households per turf, because saved walk results may be selected on who was knocked (plausible, not checked against walk data).
bearings.verifier_note: Paper numbers and the formula match the code. Corrected: the 0.5 weights are per-district defaults, not hand-set constants for all districts. The paper's warning concerns samples and years that change, not districts. Non-random selection of walk results is an inference that was not checked.

bearings.paper_claim: Policy gains are identified from randomized assignment through the AIPW score; identifying the causal effect of each covariate is not needed (Section 4.3, Appendix B). The 2014 rule's gains held in a caliper-matched 2015 sample but not in the full 2015 sample (Section 5.6, Table 8). The paper validates with 20-fold cross-validation rather than a single-look holdout (Section 5.3).
bearings.paper_location: Section 4.3, Appendix B; Section 5.3; Section 5.6, Table 8
bearings.system_side: fec/engine/outcome_contract.py fixes CLAIM_SCOPE to receptivity_forecast_only_not_spending_effects and describes itself as forecasting machinery, never spending-effect evidence. The H1 seeding and H2 pressure tests check rank correlations of frozen features with later cosponsorship and tier movement. No randomized treatment is part of the design.
bearings.transfer_conditions: The paper shows the missing design: randomized treatment within strata, which is the precondition for upgrading from forecasting to spending-effect evidence. This is feasible for Terrier contacts or CU outreach logs and not for statutory PAC contributions to legislators. The paper's gains are not evidence for the system.
bearings.verifier_note: Paper claims checked against Section 5.6, Table 8 and the Appendix B identification wording. Code scope string and H1/H2 wording verified. Equation numbers Eq. 3-4 were not re-checked. The original held only for similar units wording is replaced with the matched-versus-full-sample contrast.

bearings.paper_claim: Treating everyone as a gift recipient is net-negative or near zero: all-gift minus no-gift is +0.05 to +0.08 euro for the warm list (not significant) and -0.97 euro per donor for the cold list (significant) (Table 1). Targeted warm-list donors differ from non-targeted donors only modestly in prior giving (8-year total 130.98 vs 123.39 euro; 787 targeted vs 1,567 non-targeted; Table 4, Panel A). The paper cautions that observed characteristics are correlates of response, not the channels through which the gift works (Section 5.4).
bearings.system_side: The workbook sheet Blended Model has an Allocation column (column U) beside Rank (column T) and Score (column S). In the copy read here that column has no cached values, so the claim that the top 133 of 533 members are funded from a flat 2.0 million dollar pot was NOT reproduced. The cited producer fec/apply_alloc_cap.py does not exist in the repo.
bearings.code_ref: Moneyball Main Version - Blended.xlsx, sheet Blended Model, column U (Melange repo, read-only); fec/apply_alloc_cap.py (absent)
bearings.transfer_conditions: Conceptual only. The magnitudes come from donors, not legislators. The transferable point is to compare any proportional allocator against uniform and random benchmarks. The paper does not show that the allocator is wrong, and the system side is unverified.
bearings.verifier_note: Paper numbers verified in Table 1 and Table 4 and the Section 5.4 cautions. The system side could not be reproduced: the workbook has no cached allocation values and the cited producer file is absent. The bearing stays weak and conceptual.

related.why: Item file title matches Tappin et al. 2023 on potential persuasive returns to political microtargeting; it addresses the same benchmark-relative question in persuasion.
Item file title matches Simchon et al. 2024 on persuasive effects of political microtargeting; it parallels the policy-tree vs all-gift comparison in persuasion.

Item file title matches Kalla and Broockman, a randomized field experiment on a costly political instrument (campaign contributions and access). Both use randomized field designs for a costly political treatment.
Item file title matches Broockman and Kalla 2026 on whether moderation wins votes depending on where voters are, the same lesson that effects depend on population.
Item file title matches Madsen and Pilditch 2017, an agent-based proof of principle for micro-targeted campaigning; this paper supplies the field-experimental counterpart with net-of-cost numbers.

summary_issues: summary_md says the 2014 rule helped only where 2015 donors closely resembled 2014 donors (caliper 0.1). The paper reports significance against no-gift up to caliper radius 0.25 and says effects are not significant above 0.1; the full-sample gain is not significant.
summary_md and finding 3 call the warm-list heterogeneity loading (0.959) significant without caveat. It is significant only at the 10 percent level (p 0.088 one-sided, Table E.3).
Key finding 8 misstates the socioeconomic-only rule against no-gift: Table 6 Panel A gives 0.29 vs no-gift and 0.27 vs random-gift, not 0.27 vs no-gift.
The bearing for the competitiveness multiplier says significance against all-gift holds only up to caliper 0.1. The paper does not state that threshold (corrected in the bearing).
The paper gives the 2015 follow-up sample as 3,616 in the text and Figure H.1, but 3,612 in Table G.2. Quote figures with that inconsistency named.
The workbook-allocator system side (top 133 of 533 members, flat 2.0 million dollar pot) was not reproduced: no cached values in the Blended Model sheet and the cited producer file is absent.
Ext coverage says the text file has 4,079 lines; wc counts 4,078 lines. Trivial, but the line count should be corrected.
